Gemma 4 translates Roman Urdu best. Gemma 3 downloads in minutes and answers faster, but is less accurate.

These match the keys in the keyboard toolbar: arrows for direction, the tone key for tone. Auto picks the tone from what you wrote.
The translation shows up here. You can edit it.
The rules, example bank and spellings the model follows. Rules and examples are separate for each tone and for To English; the glossary is shared.
How the translation talks about you: \"I\'m tired\" becomes \"Main thak gaya hoon\" or \"Main thak gayi hoon\".
Example bank (input | output, one per line). For each message the keyboard picks the 6 closest.
Spelling glossary (word -> preferred spelling, one per line). Used for Roman Urdu output.
Pick a colour for the keyboard. The app follows it too. Wallpaper matches your phone, like Gboard.
Use the GPU (try this if translating is slow)
If the GPU does not work on your phone it falls back to the CPU on its own.
Translate, Casual/Formal and Auto are in the bar above the keys. The mic types what you say right in the keyboard.
The bubble above the key you touch
Get the translator ready while typing
Loads the translator after a few letters so Translate is quick. It frees that memory again after 10 minutes of not translating.
Finishes the word you are typing and fixes typos in the strip above the keys. It learns your own words (names, Roman Urdu) on this phone only, and never in password, email or address fields.
Fixes clear typos when you press space (teh becomes the, dont becomes don\'t). Press Backspace right after to undo it. It leaves names, abbreviations and anything that looks like Roman Urdu alone.
Slide your finger across the letters and lift to type a word. English words for now; tap a suggestion above the keys to change the word.
Double space types a full stop
Keeps text you copy so you can paste it again (clipboard button in the tools panel), and offers what you just copied as a Paste chip above the keys. Stays on this phone.
Number hints on the top row
The small 1 to 0; long-press a key to type it
The GIF and Sticker tabs in the emoji screen search GIPHY, over the internet. Only the words you search for are sent, never what you type in other boxes.
This version already has a GIPHY key, so GIFs work without doing anything. You can paste your own below to replace it.
GIPHY needs a free key. Make one in two minutes: open the GIPHY developer page below, sign up, tap Create an API Key, choose API, name it anything, then paste the key here.
GIFs and stickers are off until a key is added.
Free GIPHY keys allow 100 searches an hour. Results are remembered while the keyboard is open to save searches.
Keyboard: written for this app and styled after Gboard.
Translation: Google\'s Gemma 4 running on your phone through LiteRT-LM (Apache 2.0).
Icons: Material Symbols by Google (Apache 2.0). Key font: Google Sans (SIL Open Font License). Emoji list: unicode-emoji-json (MIT) from Unicode data.

Spelling data: RUWV-NSR, Roman Urdu Word Variations and Normalized Sentiment Review Dataset, by Mudasar Ahmed (Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Science and Technology). Mendeley Data, V5, doi:10.17632/v5jfhsvtmd.5. Licence CC BY 4.0. Changes: flattened into a list of spelling variant → most common spelling. It is used only to recognise different spellings of the same word: when picking examples, when detecting the language, and when applying your spelling glossary.\nhttps://data.mendeley.com/datasets/v5jfhsvtmd/5
This app is open source under GPL-3.0.\nhttps://github.com/pauldeggington/roman-urdu-keyboard
This step hit a problem. You can skip it and carry on; the details are saved under Last error in the app.
Type in English, send it in Roman Urdu. Or the other way round.
One tap on the Translate key turns your message into Roman Urdu, casual or formal.
The translator runs on your phone. What you type is never sent anywhere.
Same look and layout you know, with a Translate key on top.
Setup takes about 2 minutes. The translator is a one-time download (2.6 GB, or 0.6 GB for the smaller one), best on Wi-Fi.
A small AI model does the translating. It lives on your phone, so it works with no internet and nothing leaves your phone.
Gemma 4 E2B. Understands Roman Urdu best. No account needed.
Gemma 3 1B. Downloads fast and answers faster, but translates less accurately. Needs a free Hugging Face token.
You\'re on mobile data. Wait for Wi-Fi?
Google keeps Gemma 3 behind a licence click. It takes about a minute, once:

Tap OK on Android\'s messages, then come back here
Android warns that any keyboard could collect what you type. That\'s a standard message for every keyboard. This one works offline: your typing stays on your phone.
Pick Roman Urdu Keyboard in the list that pops up.
Later you can switch keyboards with the keyboard icon at the bottom corner of the screen, or by holding the globe key.
